chains.title: C250T creates a de novo ETS site occupied by GABPA (GABP complex), activating TERT transcription in glioblastoma

links.claim: The alt allele gains ETS-class binding: group G003 has 18/18 passing models concordant for alt binding more (best model ETV5 z 167.5, effect 2.42; site strength ref 94.8th to alt 99.9th percentile). Within this shared-specificity group I choose GABPA, not because it is the top model (it is not; ETV5, ELF1, ELF4 score higher) but because it is the only group member with direct ChIP evidence of occupancy at this exact position: two ENCODE GABPA peaks (HepG2, SK-N-SH) contain chr5:1295135, and GABPA has its own passing QBiC model (z 71.3) and is expressed in glioblastoma lines (15.5 TPM). The ChIP peaks are from wild-type, non-glioma biosamples, so they show the promoter is a GABPA-bound region, not that binding is allele-specific.

The variant lies in ENCODE cCRE EH38E3622530, a promoter-like signature with high DNase, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac (z-scores are maxima across biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific), i.e. the TERT core promoter; two flanking pELS elements are also annotated but no second native ETS site is documented in the evidence.

The variant is 0.0 kb from the TERT TSS and inside the TERT promoter cCRE, so cis action on TERT is far more likely than on CLPTM1L (50 kb) or other neighbours; this is proximity only, with no eQTL or allele-specific expression evidence cited.

GABPA is expressed in glioblastoma lines (15.5 TPM) and TERTp mutations are among the most frequent alterations in IDH-wildtype GBM, which is consistent with but does not prove cell-type-specific action here.

Literature reports that the hotspot promoter mutations C228T and C250T are recurrent across melanoma, bladder and CNS tumours and act by generating novel TF binding sites that raise TERT expression and telomerase activity; note that DepMap CRISPR shows no short-term TERT dependency in CNS lines (median -0.00), consistent with telomerase acting over many divisions rather than as an acute essential gene.

This is a binding prediction plus expression, and the evidence cannot distinguish ETS1 from ERF, ELK1/3 or ETV5.
The gained site sits in the active promoter-like cCRE of TERT; nothing in the evidence is ETS1-specific.
Occupancy at this cCRE would act on TERT, whose TSS coincides with the variant.
ETS1 is abundant in glioblastoma lines, a lineage in which TERTp mutations are frequent.
Any ETS-driven reactivation of TERT raises telomerase and supports continued proliferation in the tumour types listed.

chains.title: An ELF-class ETS factor (ELF1) with the strongest predicted gain binds the created site

links.claim: ELF1 has its own passing model in G003 (z 164.2, alt binds more), close to the group best. Groups G020 and G345 give even larger per-model effects (ELF3 effect 5.17; SPDEF 2.18) but their named factors are essentially unexpressed in glioblastoma (<0.5 TPM), so within those specificities the expressed covered members are ELF1/ELF2/ELF4. ELF1 is chosen by expression plus own-model rank; this remains a binding prediction alone with no ChIP support at this site.
The site is in the TERT promoter-like cCRE with high DNase and H3K4me3 across biosamples.
TERT is the gene whose TSS coincides with this cCRE.

ELF1 is expressed in glioblastoma lines (17.4 TPM) while the epithelial members ELF3/ELF5/SPDEF are not; the evidence contains no bladder or melanoma expression data, so lineage-specific claims cannot be made.
Increased TERT transcription from the mutant promoter sustains telomerase and tumour cell proliferation.

chains.title: Loss of a repressor interaction (MBD1) at the mutated base de-represses TERT

links.claim: MBD1 (31.5 TPM) has an own passing model predicting weaker alt binding (z -41.3, effect -1.24; ref at 100th, alt 98.6th percentile). Caveat: QBiC-SELEX models unmethylated DNA while MBD1's repressive role depends on methyl-CpG, and no methylation data are cited; the loss-of-repressor direction also runs opposite to the much larger ETS gain-of-binding signal.
The variant is in the TERT promoter cCRE; the evidence provides no CpG-island or methylation annotation for this element.
Reduced repressor occupancy at this promoter would raise TERT; no evidence cited links MBD1 to TERT.
MBD1 is expressed in glioblastoma lines; whether the TERT promoter is MBD1-repressed there is untested in the cited evidence.

De-repression of TERT would raise telomerase activity, the proposed consequence of hotspot promoter mutations; the cited literature attributes this to new TF sites and displacement of negative regulators, so a repressor-loss route is possible but not demonstrated for this base.

predictions: MBD1 or repressive marks occupy the wild-type but not the mutant allele

grades_v0.reason: G003 gives a concordant alt-gain prediction and GABPA has an own passing model (z 71.3), but this is a binding prediction alone. The GABPA/GABPB1 heterotetramer claim rests on memory, not on any cited ChIP or perturbation evidence. GABPA is also not the group's best model, and no reason in the evidence singles it out.

E03 shows the variant is in a PLS cCRE with high DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3. These are maxima over biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific. The claimed second native ETS site in the flanking pELS elements has no support.
The variant is 0.0 kb from the TERT TSS and the cCRE lists TERT as a nearby gene. That is proximity only, with no eQTL, CRISPR or allele-specific expression evidence for TERT.

GABPA expression is supported (15.5 TPM) and E04f says TERTp mutations are frequent in IDH-wt GBM. Nothing shows that the promoter is silenced without the mutation or that a single site suffices for reactivation.

E04a and E04f show that TERTp mutations are common. E04e is about USP10/FOXM1 regulating TERT and does not bear on this variant. No quote shows that this variant raises telomerase activity or immortalisation.

ETS1 is only covered through CIS-BP-mapped models and has no own passing model. The group is concordant but ETS1 was chosen mainly for its TPM. It is a binding prediction only, and ETS1 could just as well be any other group member.
The promoter-like cCRE is supported (E03), but only as epigenomic context and not specific to ETS1.
Proximity to the TERT TSS is shown (E02) but nothing links ETS1 occupancy to TERT expression.
ETS1 61 TPM is shown, and E04f supports the frequency of TERTp mutations in GBM. Neither shows that ETS1 acts at this site.
E04a and E04f support TERTp mutations being common in tumours. Nothing is specific to this variant or to ETS1.

ELF1 has an own model in G003 with z 164 and the alt allele binding more. The ELF3/SPDEF effect sizes are not evidence for ELF1, because those factors are not expressed. ELF1 is chosen by elimination within a shared-specificity group, so this is a binding prediction alone.
The cCRE is promoter-like (E03), but this is generic context with no ELF1-specific evidence.
Proximity of TERT to the variant (E02) is shown, with no functional link to ELF1.
ELF1 expression is shown (17.4 TPM) and ELF3/ELF5/SPDEF are low. The claim of greater bladder relevance is not backed by any bladder expression or evidence.
The generic TERT mutation frequency is supported (E04a/f), but nothing is specific to ELF1 or to this variant.

MBD1 has an own model with z -41 and alt binding less. The direction agrees with the claim. However, MBD1 binds methylated CpG, while QBiC-SELEX models unmethylated sequence, and no methylation data are cited. This is a prediction alone.
E03 gives no CpG-island or methylation data. The claim of a CpG-island promoter and methyl-CpG repression is uncited.
E02 shows only proximity. No evidence shows that MBD1 represses TERT here.
MBD1 expression (31.5 TPM) is shown in E09, but not that the TERT promoter is silenced or repressed through MBD1.
E04a and E04f do not support a de-repression mechanism. Moreover, ETS gain-of-function binding predictions oppose a loss-of-repressor model.

grades_final.reason: G003 shows concordant alt-gain predictions for 18/18 Ets models, and GABPA has its own passing model (z 71.3). The GABPA ChIP peaks (E16) come from wild-type, non-glioma biosamples and show no allele specificity. The choice of GABPA within the group is explained, but this is still a binding prediction plus context, with no perturbation or allele-specific evidence.

VEP and ENCODE place the variant inside promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 with high DNase, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac. The z-scores are maxima over biosamples, which the claim states. This is epigenomic context directly showing the element.
The evidence is proximity only: 0.0 kb from the TERT TSS and inside its promoter cCRE. No eQTL, allele-specific expression or perturbation evidence is cited, and the claim admits this.

GABPA expression (15.5 TPM) in glioblastoma lines and the frequency of TERTp mutations in IDH-wildtype GBM are consistent with the claim. Neither shows action of this variant or of GABPA in GBM cells, and the claim acknowledges this.

Review quotes say the hotspot mutations (C228T, C250T) recur across tumors, and the mutations raise TERT expression and telomerase via new TF sites. These are general statements and are not specific to C250T, GABPA or glioblastoma. The DepMap result (no TERT dependency) is only context. The link is literature-supported but indirect.

G003 gives a group-level alt-gain prediction, and ETS1 appears only as a CIS-BP-mapped member selected by expression (61 TPM). The evidence cannot distinguish ETS1 from other group members, so this is a binding prediction alone with no ETS1-specific evidence.
The variant lies in the active TERT promoter-like cCRE. The element link is generic and is supported by the cited VEP and ENCODE evidence.
Only proximity of the variant to the TERT TSS is cited. There is no functional link to TERT, and the evidence does not mention ETS1.
ETS1 expression in GBM lines and the frequency of TERTp mutations in GBM are consistent with the claim. Neither is specific to the variant or to ETS1 acting there.
The cited literature supports TERT reactivation by promoter mutations in general. Nothing ties it to ETS1 as the driver, so the link is only generically consistent.

ELF1 has its own passing G003 model (z 164.2, alt binds more), but this is a binding prediction alone with no ChIP or perturbation support at this site. The reason for choosing ELF1 is given (expression plus own-model rank), and the direction is consistent.
The variant sits in the TERT promoter-like cCRE with high DNase and H3K4me3 signal. This is epigenomic context that directly shows the element.
The cited evidence shows only that TERT is the nearest gene at the TSS. No functional link to ELF1 is shown.
ELF1 is expressed at 17.4 TPM in GBM lines, which is only expression context. It does not show that ELF1 acts at this site.
The cited literature shows that hotspot promoter mutations raise TERT expression, telomerase activity and poor prognosis. It does not implicate ELF1, so the link is generic.

MBD1 has an own passing model with weaker alt binding (z -41.3, effect -1.24). The model uses unmethylated DNA while MBD1 repression depends on methyl-CpG, and no methylation data are cited. The prediction runs opposite to the stronger ETS gain signal. This is a binding prediction alone.
The variant is in the TERT promoter cCRE, which is supported. No CpG-island or methylation annotation is given that would support an MBD1-relevant element.
The only evidence cited is proximity (E02). Nothing links MBD1 to TERT, and the claim itself says so.
MBD1 expression is the only thing cited. There is no evidence of MBD1-mediated repression of TERT in GBM, and the claim says it is untested.

E18e mentions displacement of negative regulators from G-quadruplexes, which is a different mechanism from MBD1. Hotspot mutations raising TERT is generally supported, but a repressor-loss route for this base is not demonstrated.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
The single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs2853669, also located in the TERT promoter, may influence telomerase activity, though its clinical relevance in GBM remains unclear.

Patients carrying the SNP and TPM on the same allele (C/C and T/C cis) had shorter overall survival than those carrying them on different alleles (T/T or T/C trans; 19 vs 25 months, p = 0.048), and TERT expression was also lower in this group (p = 0.038).
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.

The telomerase reverse transcriptase gene (TERT) is the most frequently altered gene in solid tumors, including brain tumors and GBM IDH-wildtype.
Specifically, AURKB, via REST, is recruited to TERTp MUT by TRIM28.

A growing number of recent studies suggest that the most common mutations in the TERT promoter (ATG start site -124C>T and -146C>T) are associated with increased TERT mRNA expression, telomerase activity, telomere length, and poor prognosis.

Two major hotspot TERT promoter mutations (C228T and C250T) have been reported in different malignancies such as melanoma, genitourinary cancers, CNS tumors, hepatocellular carcinoma, thyroid cancers, sarcomas, and HNCs.

These mutations promote TERT gene expression by multiple mechanisms, including the generation of novel binding sites for nuclear transcription factors, displacement of negative regulators from DNA G-quadruplexes, recruitment of epigenetic activators and disruption of long-range interactions between TERT locus and telomeres.
